reviews.text: Neat little roguelike title. Telekinesis powers allow you to break the world around you, damaging enemies and giving access to secret areas. Progression and unlocks of abilities are random enough for replayability. Story mode is interesting in that the people you help carry over.

Masterpiece of a rogue-like experience. The gameplay is very fluid and the game offers a ton of different skills to suit your playstyle. Multiple build paths keep the replayability fresh and the story grips you into multiple hours of gameplay.
Surprisingly fun game. Good atmosphere, solid mechanics, and just the right amount of challenge. Not perfect, but easy to get hooked once you start playing

The special ability picks up objects to throw them. There is a part that takes place on a large wooden bridge, and the pieces of wood count as objects. I was surrounded by enemies, so I charged up my attack to get rid of them all, taking lots of woods. Some enemies were standing on top of the ones I got, so they fell into the void and I got rid of them in an instant. But I also picked up wood from where I was standing, so we all fell into the void because of my greed. 10/10

It's an interesting roguelite proposal where gamefeel plays a very important role, and it seems to deliver in that aspect. Although being in early access, I hope they continue improving user feedback when using abilities and understanding everything happening on screen. The system for obtaining active and passive abilities and powers offers great variety and replayability. Even in early access, its current state already includes the main story and very solid gameplay. Recommended, and looking forward to future updates 😊

An interesting setup moving through more traditional dungeon maps rather than the wide open fields or small arenas I've seen in most games leaning into Bullet Heaven/Survivor-like mechanics. Definitely some wide variance between ability sets that can make good runs feel excitingly powerful. On one run it seemed to take multiple minutes to take out the first miniboss, while on another I nearly melted them with energy chains bound to my thrown objects. Definitely curious to see more!

Right from the start, the atmosphere drew me in dark, mysterious, full of small visual details that make the world feel alive. Each area feels carefully designed, and the art style gives everything a striking, almost haunting beauty. The gameplay is smooth and responsive, with combat that flows naturally and encourages experimentation. It’s easy to get lost in the rhythm of fights and exploration without even noticing the time pass. Even in early access, it already feels polished and full of potential. If the developers keep improving it, this could easily become one of the standout action RPGs of the genre.
Great roguelike game! many elements can determine your gameplay not just the random skill per level upp.

Fantastic title. Lots of describable elements in the game that can work to your advantage. Takes a moment to find your play style, but once you got it, you lock in. Highly recommended if you are into rouge-lite titles.

Masks of the Void: Origins delivers an energetic blend of action and roguelite mechanics while placing an unusual emphasis on telekinetic combat instead of traditional hack-and-slash gameplay. Rather than simply equipping stronger weapons and attacking head-on, players are encouraged to manipulate the battlefield itself, turning loose objects, debris, and environmental hazards into powerful tools of destruction. This creative approach immediately gives the game its own identity, making every encounter feel more dynamic and unpredictable than many titles within the genre. The world is built around the mysterious power of ancient masks and a looming supernatural catastrophe, providing an intriguing backdrop for both its action and storytelling. Developed by ROLLDBOX GAMES and published by Forthright Entertainment, the game aims to combine satisfying gameplay with meaningful narrative progression. Combat is easily the game's biggest attraction. The telekinetic abilities allow players to launch enemies, throw massive objects, and creatively use their surroundings to overcome increasingly dangerous encounters. Instead of relying on repetitive attack chains, battles reward experimentation and quick thinking. Environmental awareness becomes just as important as character upgrades, encouraging players to constantly adapt to changing situations. The result is combat that remains engaging throughout multiple runs, with plenty of opportunities to discover new strategies and devastating combinations. Like many successful roguelites, progression revolves around repeated attempts that gradually strengthen the player through permanent unlocks and randomized rewards. Ancient masks introduce a variety of unique abilities that can dramatically change how each run unfolds, while relics and upgrades create countless build possibilities. Some runs may emphasize aggressive offensive power, while others reward defensive tactics or enhanced telekinetic efficiency. Because upgrades are randomized, every expedition presents new opportunities to experiment, adding substantial replay value without making individual runs feel identical. The game's narrative also stands out by taking a larger role than is typical for the genre. Players control Iret, a young woman whose mysterious connection to the Void places her at the center of an unfolding crisis threatening the entire world. Throughout the adventure, difficult decisions influence the direction of the story while exploring themes such as sacrifice, responsibility, and the temptation of absolute power. These narrative choices add emotional weight to the journey, ensuring that progression feels driven by more than simply collecting stronger abilities or surviving another dungeon. Visually, Masks of the Void: Origins embraces a stylized fantasy aesthetic that successfully balances vibrant magical effects with darker supernatural environments. Ancient ruins, fractured landscapes, and eerie dimensions create an atmosphere filled with mystery, while enemy designs reinforce the sense that players are venturing into a dangerous and corrupted realm. The particle effects generated by telekinetic attacks are particularly impressive, making large-scale battles feel spectacular without sacrificing clarity during fast-paced encounters. Replayability remains one of the game's strongest qualities thanks to its combination of randomized progression, multiple build paths, and flexible combat mechanics. The three distinct gameplay archetypes encourage players to approach challenges differently with each attempt, while the constantly changing upgrades prevent the experience from becoming predictable. Mastering the game's systems requires patience and experimentation, but success feels genuinely rewarding as players gradually learn how to maximize the potential of both their character and the environment. The game is not without minor shortcomings. Because roguelite progression depends heavily on randomized rewards, some runs naturally feel more effective than others depending on upgrade availability. Likewise, larger battles can occasionally become visually chaotic as enemies, environmental objects, and telekinetic effects fill the screen simultaneously. Fortunately, these issues rarely overshadow the game's core strengths, as the satisfying combat mechanics and rewarding progression continue to provide compelling reasons to jump into another run. Masks of the Void: Origins succeeds by offering an inventive interpretation of the action roguelite formula. Its emphasis on physics-driven telekinetic combat, meaningful character progression, replayable build diversity, and story-focused adventure creates an experience that feels both familiar and refreshingly original. Players looking for a roguelite that encourages creativity as much as combat skill will find plenty to appreciate here, especially if they enjoy experimenting with unconventional abilities and environmental interactions. With its distinctive gameplay systems and engaging presentation. Rating: 9/10
